verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — the spec covers download, the 60s benchmark, and header-only empty output, but it sends the widgets CSV column row to acme/mailer, so the widgets export's contents are left unspecified in widgets.
findings:
- [blocker] scope @ "The CSV contains id, name, and status columns in that order. - elsewhere: acme/mailer" — In Human input this row sits under the `### acme/widgets` heading, which is this repo (acme/widgets). It does not sit under a group naming another repo, so `elsewhere:` is not allowed here. Mailer never produces the CSV, so delegating its columns there leaves the widgets download with no defined contents. → Change the disposition to `in-scope` and specify the header `id,name,status` in that order in Design. — probed: Human input `### acme/widgets` group vs. spec AC row - row is listed under acme/widgets, not acme/mailer
- [blocker] gap @ Design "Column selection is assigned to mailer" — The Design defines the widgets export endpoint but gives its columns to mailer. The implementer cannot know what columns the widgets CSV should hold, and "write the header even when no rows exist" has no defined header. → Replace with "Columns are id, name, status in that order; the header row is always written." — probed: none
- [major] ambiguity @ Goal "This change delivers all four widgets rows." — This contradicts the AC table, which marks only three widgets rows `in-scope` and one widgets row `elsewhere`. → Fix the disposition per the first finding so all four widgets rows are `in-scope`, which makes the Goal statement true. — probed: none
- [major] ambiguity @ Verification "Request tests check the download headers, column order and CSV escaping" — Widgets tests verify column order for a row the spec marks `elsewhere`. Either the disposition or the test is wrong. → Keep the column-order test and make the row `in-scope`. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope" — The row is unconditionally `in-scope`, so "when in-scope" is a dead conditional. The benchmark's environment and pass criterion are also unstated: hardware/CI runner, DB seeding, and whether it is a gating test. → Drop "when in-scope". State where the benchmark runs and that exceeding 60s fails it. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification "CSV escaping" — No escaping rules are defined in Design. It does not say how commas, quotes, newlines, and nulls in name/status are handled, or whether a BOM or CRLF line endings are used. → Add "RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF line endings, no BOM, nulls as empty fields" (or the chosen rules) to Design. — probed: none
